rationale: Round 0 built cleanly with correct execution, so this candidate escalates obfuscation strength across the board while keeping risk weights low. The program is a tiny symbolic-differentiator (19 functions, ~4.4 KB text) whose largest bodies are recursive deriv() methods with polymorphic dispatch; FLA is weighted highest to destroy the control-flow structure of those large recursive deriv/print functions, and SUB is weighted strongly on Security/Diversity because instruction substitution is nearly free and compounds with every other pass in these arithmetic-heavy expression routines. BCF gets elevated opaque-predicate weighting since the negligible runtime of the benchmark tolerates bogus-flow overhead, while IBR adds block-order randomization on top of flattening to resist pattern-matching of flattened dispatchers. ICALL is favored because the code is already vtable-driven, so converting remaining direct calls to indirect ones blends naturally with the existing dispatch surface; IGV and SPLIT are moderate contributors — SPLIT mainly to create extra basic blocks for FLA/IBR to scramble, IGV to obscure the small set of globals used in parsing. All CorrectnessRisk weights stay ≤0.2 to preserve the clean round-0 build and run, with ICALL and IGV watched most closely as the only passes with meaningful semantic hazard.
